sample.summary: After Elizabeth rejects his proposal, Mr. Collins still plans to remain at Longbourn until Saturday. The next morning, the Bennet sisters walk to Meryton, meet Mr. Wickham, and return with him and another officer to Longbourn, where Wickham is introduced to Mr. and Mrs. Bennet. Shortly after their arrival, Jane receives a letter from Caroline Bingley announcing that the entire Netherfield party has departed for London to join Charles Bingley with no intention of returning for the winter, and expressing hope that Charles will marry Georgiana Darcy. Throughout the morning, Mr. Collins treats Elizabeth with resentful silence and transfers his attentions to Charlotte Lucas, while Mrs. Bennet remains ill-humored. On the walk from Meryton, Wickham tells Elizabeth he voluntarily skipped the Netherfield ball to avoid an unpleasant encounter with Mr. Darcy, a decision Elizabeth approves. Upstairs at Longbourn, Jane reads Caroline's letter aloud and concludes that Bingley is indifferent to her. Elizabeth counters that Bingley loves Jane and that Caroline is deliberately trying to keep him in London to separate them and promote a marriage with Miss Darcy. Unwilling to believe Caroline is deceitful, Jane hopes Caroline is simply mistaken, and Elizabeth gradually convinces her that Bingley will return. Afterward, Jane and Elizabeth inform Mrs. Bennet only of the family's departure from Netherfield without mentioning Caroline's remarks about Bingley's affections. Mrs. Bennet laments the sudden trip at length, then consoles herself by assuming Bingley will soon return and planning a two-course dinner for him at Longbourn.
sample.synopsis: Wickham visits Longbourn while Collins snubs Elizabeth for Charlotte. Caroline Bingley's letter announces the Netherfield party left for London, though Elizabeth convinces Jane that Bingley will return.

sample.summary:
During the militia regiment's final week in Meryton, Mrs. Bennet, Kitty, and Lydia openly grieve the officers' impending departure. Lydia's distress ends when Colonel Forster's young wife invites her to accompany them to Brighton. While Lydia and Mrs. Bennet celebrate, Kitty complains bitterly about being excluded. Later, on the regiment's last day in town, Mr. Wickham and other officers dine at Longbourn, after which Lydia departs with Mrs. Forster to begin her trip the next morning.

Appalled by Lydia's unchecked behavior, Elizabeth privately urges Mr. Bennet to forbid the Brighton trip, warning him that Lydia's wildness and lack of restraint will damage the entire family's respectability and corrupt Kitty further. Mr. Bennet dismisses her concerns, arguing that Longbourn will have no peace if Lydia stays, that Colonel Forster will keep her from real harm, and that Brighton will teach her insignificance. Disappointed, Elizabeth accepts his decision. At the farewell dinner, Elizabeth represses Wickham's renewed romantic attentions. When he asks about her time at Hunsford, she deliberately mentions spending three weeks with Mr. Darcy and Colonel Fitzwilliam, adding that Darcy's disposition is better understood upon closer acquaintance. Alarmed and agitated, Wickham attributes Darcy's good behavior to his fear of Lady Catherine and desire to marry Miss de Bourgh. Elizabeth smiles, refuses to engage further, and parts from him with polite indifference.

Unaware of Elizabeth's attempt to stop the journey, Lydia leaves home in noisy excitement, encouraged by Mrs. Bennet to enjoy herself and envied by a weeping Kitty.
sample.synopsis: Mrs. Forster invites Lydia to Brighton. Elizabeth urges Mr. Bennet to forbid the trip, warning of family disgrace, but he refuses. Elizabeth rebuffs Wickham at dinner, and Lydia departs.

sample.summary: While the centralcourtship arcs sustain relentless causal momentum, secondary threads—such as Colonel Fitzwilliam's flirtation, Wickham's pursuit of Mary King, and the Georgiana-Bingley matchmaking scheme—are compressed or quietly dropped the moment their immediate catalytic pressure on Elizabeth is spent. Even late-stage developments like Charlotte's pregnancy and flight to Lucas Lodge exit on brisk transitional beats rather than receiving final epilogue timing.

firstFinding.headline: Lydia's early infatuation with Captain Carter is introduced and dropped without payoff once Wickham arrives
bullets: Captain Carter is established as Lydia's primary romantic fixation in Meryton, with Lydia anticipating his return from London.
After Wickham enters the regiment, Captain Carter never reappears or receives mention again, functioning purely as an early marker of Lydia's interchangeable obsession with officers.
